targets.approach: Preferred approach: from the small parking area at the end of the dirt road above the condos below the Sherwins, climb straight up the slope to the hiking trail, turn left to the Mammoth Rock trail, then leave the trail toward the rock. Take a clear shelf toward the big golden talus field and follow mixed talus and steep slopes up to the rock. Once in the chute, zigzag one long switchback to the left and then right to reach the wall's foot. Gas Is King is the furthest-right route on the crag.
targets.name: Gas is King

targets.approach: Preferred approach: from the small parking area at the end of the dirt road above the condos below the Sherwins, climb straight up the slope to the hiking trail, turn left to the Mammoth Rock trail, then leave the trail toward the rock. Take a clear shelf toward the big golden talus field and follow mixed talus and steep slopes up to the rock. Once in the chute, zigzag one long switchback to the left and then right to reach the wall's foot. None Like It Hot is the easiest-looking crack, right of center, and is the first route you reach; it ends at a one-bolt arete and a two-bolt anchor.
targets.name: None Like It Hot

targets.approach: Preferred approach: from the small parking area at the end of the dirt road above the condos below the Sherwins, climb straight up the slope to the hiking trail, turn left to the Mammoth Rock trail, then leave the trail toward the rock. Take a clear shelf toward the big golden talus field and follow mixed talus and steep slopes up to the rock. Once in the chute, zigzag one long switchback to the left and then right to reach the wall's foot. Nuclear Option is in the middle of the wall, marked by obvious dikes and bolts.
targets.name: Nuclear Option

targets.approach: Preferred approach: from the small parking area at the end of the dirt road above the condos below the Sherwins, climb straight up the slope to the hiking trail, turn left to the Mammoth Rock trail, then leave the trail toward the rock. Take a clear shelf toward the big golden talus field and follow mixed talus and steep slopes up to the rock. Once in the chute, zigzag one long switchback to the left and then right to reach the wall's foot. Petrol Head is on the right half of the crag, right of the warm-up crack None Like It Hot.
targets.name: Petrol Head

targets.approach: Preferred approach: from the small parking area at the end of the dirt road above the condos below the Sherwins, climb straight up the slope to the hiking trail, turn left to the Mammoth Rock trail, then leave the trail toward the rock. Take a clear shelf toward the big golden talus field and follow mixed talus and steep slopes up to the rock. Once in the chute, zigzag one long switchback to the left and then right to reach the wall's foot. Plastic Fantastic is the furthest-left line on the crag, following the clear dihedral and splitter crack.
targets.descent_text: Lower from the two-bolt anchor, which has lowering biners.
targets.name: Plastic Fantastic

targets.approach: Cross Taboose Pass to the John Muir Trail, then go north on it to the crossing of the South Fork of the Kings River. Shortly past the crossing a use trail heads southwest toward Cartridge Pass. Follow its faint tread past some lakes and over the low point between Cirque Crest and Mt. Ruskin, then down past the lakes until the Hershey's Kiss face appears; there are good campsites along the lakes. Wonka's Way goes up the left portion of the main steep face, immediately right of the broken lower-angle gullies, and starts on low-angle slabs below a large left-facing corner.
targets.name: Wonka's Way

targets.approach: Starting in the Lakes Basin, cross the ridge and descend the gully; the wall towers on the gully's east side. Swish Dike climbs straight toward the face's high point, which lies left of center.
targets.name: Swish Dike

targets.approach: Park at the Lake George lot and take the Crystal Lake trail; at the Crystal Lake sign, turn left and descend to the lake. Walk around the lake, and a little farther on, a climbers trail branches left to the foot of the cliff. Highlands Wall is the first cliff reached, a northeast-facing wall visible from the parking lot.
targets.name: Islay

targets.approach: Park at the Lake George lot and take the Crystal Lake trail; at the Crystal Lake sign, turn left and descend to the lake. Walk around the lake, and a little farther on, a climbers trail branches left to the foot of the cliff. Highlands Wall is the first cliff reached, a northeast-facing wall visible from the parking lot. The route begins in the large chimney at the far left end of the wall, with the bolted crystal-dike route You Only Live Twice on its left and No Time To Die on its right.
targets.name: Northeast Buttress

targets.approach: Park at the Lake George lot and take the Crystal Lake trail; at the Crystal Lake sign, turn left and descend to the lake. Walk around the lake, and a little farther on, a climbers trail branches left to the foot of the cliff. Highlands Wall is the first cliff reached, a northeast-facing wall visible from the parking lot. You Only Live Twice follows a bolted crystal dike just left of the large chimney at the wall's far left end.
targets.name: You Only Live Twice

targets.approach: The route is on the right side of the wall in the Hinterland and climbs through some of the larger roofs.
targets.name: Beggars Banquet

targets.approach: Go up the Hinterland Gully. Before scrambling up to the large ledge below the route Autopia, start in a recess off the left-hand gully. The climb works up short dihedrals to the main ledge and finishes at the anchor shared with Autopia.
targets.name: Big Thunder

targets.approach: Go high up the Hinterland Gully to the south side of its left flank; the climb starts in a left-facing corner, at the same start as Ridgeback.
targets.descent_text: From the bushy ledge at the top of the second pitch, head west along the ledge to trees under Ridgeback, then rappel off those trees into a loose gully.
targets.name: Breathing Space

targets.approach: The route starts in the middle of the wall at the Hinterland and follows a line of weakness through the overlapping exfoliation slabs, angling slightly right to halfway and then going straight up.
targets.name: Humble Pie

targets.approach: Climb the Hinterland Gully as far as the foot of Crest of the Far East, then follow the base of the formation south to its left side, where the route begins on slabs.
targets.name: Layer Cake

targets.approach: The route is on the far left side of Hinterland Wall and begins in a left-facing dihedral.
targets.descent_text: The top anchor has rappel hangers that are not suitable for lowering, so rappel only. For a rappel of just the first pitch, use the anchor left of the trees.
targets.name: Aquarium

targets.approach: The route is on Hinterland Wall and shares its first-pitch dihedral start with the route Aquarium, at the far left side of the wall.
targets.name: Natural Mystic

targets.approach: From the Tahquitz north gully trail, a mostly level trail splits south toward the Diamondback routes. At the Diamondback buttress, go uphill west for several hundred feet to a group of large pines; Hondo Buttress faces north, just west of Diamondback's descent. Free starts by a big pine where a gully begins; a granite block there makes a comfy seat. Scramble up that gully to where the rock gets steeper.
targets.name: Free

targets.approach: From the Tahquitz north gully trail, a mostly level trail splits south toward the Diamondback routes. At the Diamondback buttress, go uphill west for several hundred feet to a group of large pines; Hondo Buttress faces north, just west of Diamondback's descent. Hondo Hedral climbs the visor that arches left, beside a big pine.
targets.name: Hondo Hedral

targets.approach: From the Tahquitz north gully trail, a mostly level trail splits south toward the Diamondback routes. At the Diamondback buttress, go uphill west for several hundred feet to a group of large pines; Hondo Buttress faces north, just west of Diamondback's descent. Rider starts in the gap between the pines and goes up a ramp to the smaller of two laybacks.
targets.name: Rider

targets.approach: Hike to Iceberg Lake in the cirque above Whitney Portal, go around the lake, and work up the loose slope to the cliff bands, which sit to the north and northeast of the lake. The route starts in a large notch in the middle of the boulder pile.
targets.name: Evelyn's Playground

targets.approach: Hike to Iceberg Lake in the cirque above Whitney Portal, go around the lake, and work up the loose slope to the cliff bands, which sit to the north and northeast of the lake. The route is on the tower just right of center on the western crag, which is the left-hand crag as seen from camp.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the tower from a sling on a horn at the summit. Traversing the ridge east or west to descend looks possible but complicated.
targets.name: Iceberg Lake Gear Exchange

targets.approach: Hike to Iceberg Lake in the cirque above Whitney Portal, go around the lake, and work up the loose slope to the cliff bands, which sit to the north and northeast of the lake. The route is on the ragged cliff band along the lake's northeast side; skirt the lake's east shore and climb the scree below to the foot of the route.
targets.descent_text: A rappel from the notch at the top reaches the ground.
targets.name: Left-Leaning Crack

targets.approach: Hike to Iceberg Lake in the cirque above Whitney Portal, go around the lake, and work up the loose slope to the cliff bands, which sit to the north and northeast of the lake. Look for a big chimney shaped like the letter A at the right end of the lower cliff; the route enters it from the bottom and follows the crack system above all the way to the summit.
targets.name: The "EH" Team

targets.approach: Follow the north talus approach to Tahquitz's north face and the North Gully descent, then continue much farther. The Indian Buttress formation lies just beyond the Hinterland cirque, deep in the cirque known as the Others.
targets.name: Indian Summer

targets.approach: Starting in Miter Basin, ascend the drainage below Iridescent Lake over gentle slabs and grassy meadows. At the outlet, skirt the east shore, get past a short third-class step, and take ledges up to the wall. Buns Of Steel breaches the headwall of the main tower.
targets.descent_text: Either rappel the neighbouring route Civilized or walk off.
targets.name: Buns Of Steel

targets.approach: Starting in Miter Basin, ascend the drainage below Iridescent Lake over gentle slabs and grassy meadows. At the outlet, skirt the east shore, get past a short third-class step, and take ledges up to the wall. Civilized starts at a V-shaped crack in the middle of the white tower.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route. All the anchors are two-bolt stations with links.
targets.name: Civilized

targets.approach: Starting in Miter Basin, ascend the drainage below Iridescent Lake over gentle slabs and grassy meadows. At the outlet, skirt the east shore, get past a short third-class step, and take ledges up to the wall. The route lies at the right of the white triangular pillar that makes up the wall's left portion. Two chimney features sit at the base; the first pitch starts up the side of the right-hand chimney.
targets.descent_text: To rappel the route, stop at the final bolted anchor, at the right edge of the pillar's top. The headwall above adds a short stretch to the true top.
targets.name: Iridescent Flow

targets.approach: Approach as for the Rock Craft formation, then take a faint path heading down and east to the White Fang formation. The crack is on the south face, at the rock's lower side toward the hill.
targets.name: White Fang Crack

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. This route is on Mega Dome, uphill and southeast of base camp, and takes the crack and ramp system left of the huge roof on the dome's north face.
targets.descent_text: After the last pitch, belay on the slabs above, walk the ridge east and rappel from slings on the north side of the dome.
targets.name: Bigger than Life

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. The line follows the long, rounded arete just north of the formation that carries an obvious V-shaped feature, finishing in a crack system right of the arete.
targets.name: California Dreamin'

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. It starts on the northwest arete of the shark-fin dome that sits above and south of Mega Dome.
targets.name: Digitally Remastered

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. The line takes the arete that has a prominent roof or arch partway up it.
targets.name: If 60's were 90's

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. The route is on Sugar Pine Dome itself and climbs a left-facing chimney to a bolted belay.
targets.descent_text: Rappel south from the bolted belay.
targets.name: Sugar Pine Dome Unfinished Climb!

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. The route climbs the knife-edge arete on the south face of Sugar Pine Dome, starting with a layback off the ground into a corner.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route with a single rope to the ground.
targets.name: The Edge of Sanity

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. It lies on the formation with the V-shaped feature, just south of California Dreamin', and takes the right-hand crack; belay below the roof and traverse left under it.
targets.name: 'V'

targets.approach: From the dirt turnout on Chimney Peak Road, follow the ridge northeast of the turnout up to the foot of Sugar Pine Dome, the prominent dome with a big pine at its base. That spot is the usual base camp, but there is no water, so carry it in. The other domes lie a further short walk from there. The route is on the longest arete here, recognisable by a long right-facing dihedral low on the line; it is not quite the northernmost crag.
targets.name: Waiting to Exhale
